title: Approval-gated transfer — pending request created, asset not moved until decision
objective: Verify that when the transfer transition rule requires approval, POST transfer creates an ApprovalRequest (pending_approval) and the asset does not enter In Transit until approved.
preconditions: Transfer transition rule with requires_approval enabled (seed/config); transferable asset; requester (operator/manager) + approver (deptmgr+) users.
steps: POST /assets/<uuid>/transfer as requester.
Verify response indicates pending approval and asset status unchanged.
GET /approvals as approver — verify request listed with type, requester, asset, reason, payload summary.
Verify the request is NOT listed (or is scope-hidden) for an out-of-scope approver.
expected_result: Transfer deferred behind pending ApprovalRequest; no side effects on the asset pre-decision; inbox visibility scoped to eligible approvers (DeptManager+ per route table); request payload contains proposed changes + reason.

title: Approve — decision executes underlying action with comments and audit linkage
objective: Verify POST /approvals/:uuid/approve records the decision (approver, decided_at, comments), executes the underlying action (transfer proceeds to In Transit / disposal executes), and links audit events.
test_data: approve payload {comments 'Approved for Q4 move'}; Idempotency-Key
steps: POST /api/v1/approvals/<uuid>/approve as eligible approver.
Verify approval status/decided_at/approver/comments persisted.
Verify underlying action executed (transfer status in_transit; asset updated).
Verify lifecycle + audit events reference the approval (correlation).
expected_result: Approval decision immutable-recorded; action executes atomically with the decision (no half-state on failure); events traceable both directions; replay with same Idempotency-Key does not double-execute.

title: Reject and return-for-changes — no side effects, comments required/recorded
objective: Verify reject and return endpoints record the decision with comments and leave the underlying asset/request payload unchanged; requester can see the outcome.
preconditions: Two pending approval requests (one to reject, one to return).
test_data: reject {comments 'Not cost-justified'}; return {comments 'Please split into two transfers'}
steps: POST reject on request A; verify status rejected + comments; asset unchanged.
POST return on request B; verify status returned + comments; asset unchanged.
Verify requester visibility of both outcomes (inbox/notification when delivered).
expected_result: Both decisions recorded immutably with comments; zero mutation to target assets; request state machine consistent (decided requests no longer actionable).

title: Separation of duties — requester cannot approve own request when enabled
objective: Verify that when SoD is enabled, the requester (even with approver role) cannot decide their own request (403 with stable code); when disabled, behavior matches config documentation.
preconditions: SoD config enabled; a user holding both requester and approver capabilities creates a request.
test_data: self-approval attempt; another approver as control
steps: As the requester-approver user, POST approve on own request → record status/code.
As a different eligible approver, approve → success control.
Verify audit trail shows SoD denial.
expected_result: Self-approval rejected (403 PERMISSION_DENIED or dedicated stable code) with user-safe message; independent approver succeeds; denial audited; config-off behavior documented if tested.

title: Approval history immutable after decision
objective: Verify decided approvals cannot be re-decided, edited, or deleted; history (request + decision + comments) is preserved and readable by authorized roles.
preconditions: One approved and one rejected request.
steps: Attempt to approve an already-approved request → expect 409.
Attempt reject on a rejected request → expect 409.
Attempt PATCH/DELETE on the approval resource → expect 404/405.
GET approval detail → full history intact.
expected_result: Re-decision blocked with stable 409 code; no mutation surface; request + decision + comments preserved verbatim; history included in audit trail.

title: Approval inbox authorization — role + scope filtering
objective: Verify GET /approvals lists only requests the user is eligible to decide (DeptManager+ within scope; admin/manager per capability map); employee/operator/auditor receive 403 or empty-scoped lists per contract; direct access to out-of-scope request → 404.
preconditions: Pending requests in dept A and dept B; deptmgr-A, deptmgr-B, operator, employee, auditor, admin sessions.
test_data: GET /approvals per role; direct GET/decision attempts on cross-scope request uuid
steps: List inbox as each role; record contents/status.
deptmgr-A attempts to approve dept-B request → expect 404.
employee/auditor attempts → expect 403.
expected_result: Inbox scoped correctly; cross-scope decision attempts → 404 (ADR-007); insufficient roles → 403; no payload details leaked in error bodies.

title: E2E — approval inbox UI: list, review payload, decide with comments
objective: UI journey: approver opens /approvals, reviews a pending transfer request (asset, requester, proposed change, reason), approves with comment; requester sees outcome; decided item leaves the actionable inbox.
preconditions: Full stack; Playwright; pending request; approver + requester credentials.
steps: Sign in as approver; open /approvals; verify list shows request with context.
Open detail/dialog; verify proposed-change diff + reason rendered safely.
Approve with comment; verify success only after server confirm; item removed/marked decided.
As requester: verify outcome visible (inbox/notification).
expected_result: Inbox matches API truth; decision flow per §8.5 (confirm dialog, no optimistic completion); scope/role hiding in UI mirrors backend; evidence screenshots captured.
